site.flow.line2: and CDelivery takes care of the rest
site.flow.description: App deployment, service monitoring, log and metric collection, configuration distribution, HTTPS, and load balancing—all handled automatically.
site.flow.summary: XHealth runs configured periodic checks. When enabled, Guardian validates new versions before release. Pingress routes visitors to your app. Insight collects metrics, application logs, and access records.
site.flow.topology: Three app nodes are shown inside a server cluster. XHealth runs configured periodic checks, while Guardian validates candidate versions before release when enabled. Pingress connects to all three apps, with each request shown visiting the middle app. The apps, XHealth, and Pingress continuously send data to Insight.

site.home.description: CDelivery is a self-hosted operations platform for deploying applications, managing domains and TLS, scheduling jobs, and viewing logs and metrics.
site.safety.title:
Operate with confidence
Release with confidence
site.safety.operationsBody: Beyond checking whether your app is online, regular automated checks verify critical business flows, such as user login.
site.safety.releasesBody: During a release, an isolated environment is first created in production, where validation runs automatically. Problems are caught and blocked before they cause production incidents.
site.observability.title: Observability, 100x cheaper than Datadog
site.observability.intro: Ready out of the box. No SDK needed. Automatically collect server and app metrics and logs, with long-term storage on disk or object stores like S3. New data can be ready to query and analyze in as little as 3 seconds.
site.observability.costBody: 1 GB of logs a day. 365 GB a year. Just $7.23 for the first year.
site.observability.performanceBody:
Measured throughput of {{throughput}} MB/s, with peak memory usage of just {{memory}} GiB.
Multiple instances and high availability help you keep up as your user base and data grow.
site.observability.chartDescription: Log ingestion throughput: {{throughput}} MB/s. Peak server memory: {{memory}} MiB. {{indexes}} indexes on an {{cores}}-core AWS EC2 {{instance}}.
site.observability.periodTotal: Estimated total for the first {{months}} months (USD)
site.observability.periodTotalOne: Estimated total for the first {{months}} month (USD)
site.observability.noScript: Enable JavaScript to adjust this estimate. Default costs are shown below.
site.observability.storageFees: CDelivery includes compressed S3 Standard storage in US East (N. Virginia), using monthly averages and tiered rates of $0.021–$0.023/GiB/month, plus one PUT per 16 MB at $0.005 per 1,000 requests.
site.observability.datadogFees: Datadog uses annual-plan rates: $0.10/GB ingested. One month uses Standard at $2.50/million indexed logs with 30-day retention; longer periods use Flex Starter at $0.60/million stored logs/month, based on monthly averages.
site.observability.flexLimits: Flex supports 3, 6, 12 or 15 months, fewer than 2 billion logs ingested per month and up to 10 billion stored. Other settings are extrapolated. Estimates exclude servers, reads, transfer, taxes, discounts and free allowances.
site.observability.assumptions: Estimates cover the selected retention period, starting from empty storage with steady ingestion. One month = 365/12 days; input units are decimal and S3 storage uses GiB.
site.observability.metricsCost: Metrics for one server or app: just $0.6758 a year.
site.gateway.title:
High-performance gateway.
Less hassle. Lower costs.
site.gateway.intro: CDelivery builds its reverse proxy gateway on Cloudflare’s {{pingora}}. Proven at scale on Cloudflare’s network, Pingora provides a mature, stable, and reliable foundation.
site.gateway.operations: Ready out of the box, with multiple instances for high availability and automatic HTTPS certificate management for both single-instance and multi-instance deployments.
site.xconfig.title: Build and run highly available apps that scale with ease
site.xconfig.description: Distribute configuration to multiple service instances with the same ease as local development, without learning a new stack or integrating an SDK. Run multiple instances and scale out easily, without a separate configuration service to maintain. With XHealth, services using a new configuration pass checks before going live. Scale seamlessly from one user to a billion.
site.ai.title: AI diagnostics, proactive monitoring
site.ai.context: CDelivery brings together runtime metrics, application logs, access records, and operation events, giving AI the context to analyze issues and assist with diagnosis. It includes an AI assistant and supports connecting your preferred AI tools through MCP and API access.
site.ai.duty: With AI duty enabled, CDelivery uses change events and scheduled checks to assess system health, analyze anomalies and potential risks, and proactively notify you according to your chosen policy.

site.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
site.faq.capacity.question: How many servers can CDelivery support?
site.faq.capacity.answer: You can start with just 1 server. CDelivery itself does not impose a limit on the number of servers. A single cluster can scale to 5,000 servers, comparable to the node count officially supported by Kubernetes.
site.faq.kubernetes.question: Why choose CDelivery over Kubernetes?
site.faq.kubernetes.answer: Because your team’s time and energy are better spent on your product. CDelivery brings application deployment, HTTPS, logs and metrics, business workflow checks, and release validation together in one platform, reducing the work of choosing tools, integrating components, and keeping everything running. Start with a single server and expand to multiple nodes as your business grows, without dedicated Kubernetes operations staff. Safer deployments. Simpler operations.

site.privacy.description: This policy covers visits to cdelivery.dev and correspondence with the CDelivery project. Self-hosted installations are managed by their operators.
site.privacy.hostingBody: Cloudflare delivers and protects this website. Providing these services may involve processing IP addresses, request information and traffic data. Cloudflare describes its processing in its privacy policy. Visiting this website does not require creating an account.
site.privacy.preferencesBody: The documentation may remember display preferences in your browser’s local storage, which you can clear in browser settings. Hosting security features may also use cookies. See Cloudflare’s privacy information for details.
site.privacy.correspondenceBody: When you email us, we use your email address and the information in your message to handle your enquiry. GitHub submissions are handled on GitHub, and public issues can be read by others. Third-party websites linked here have their own privacy policies.
site.privacy.instancesBody: The operator of a self-hosted installation manages its accounts, application data, logs, storage and access. Any model provider, messaging platform or storage service connected to that installation is governed by the operator’s configuration and the relevant provider’s policies. This website policy does not replace those arrangements.
site.privacy.questionsBody: Contact us about this policy or information you have sent to the project. Avoid including passwords, API keys or sensitive business data in your message.
